paraphrase: The Akulavīra is not in the supports or aims, not in the heart, mouth, uvula or palate, not in iḍā or piṅgalā, not in the navel, throat or head, not in opening the eyes or gazing at the nose-tip, not in inhalation, retention or exhalation, not in piercing the bindu or the knots, not in invocation or dismissal, postures or seals; neither near nor far, full nor empty — where there is no aim (lakṣya), that is called the Akulavīra.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: One who abides thus in samarasa is Brahmā, Hari, Īśa and Rudra, Īśvara and Śiva, the supreme god, sun, moon and fire; he is Sāṃkhya and the Purāṇas, the Arhat and the Buddha; himself goddess and god, himself disciple and guru, himself meditation and meditator, himself the deity everywhere.

original.text: यस्यैवं संस्थितं कश्चित् समरस संस्थितः । स ब्रह्मा सो हरिश्चेशः स रुद्रो स च ईश्वरः स शिवः परमदेवः स सोमार्काग्निकस्तथा । स च साङ्ख्यः पुराणाश्च अर्हन्तबुद्ध एव च स्वयं देवी स्वयं देवः स्वयं शिष्यः स्वयं गुरुः । स्वयं ध्यानं स्वयं ध्याता स्वयं सर्वत्र देवता
original.edition: Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: Whatever disposition a person constantly cultivates, that fruit he obtains; there is no need to deliberate on the matter.

original.text: यादृशेन तु भावेन पुरुषो भावयेत् सदा । तादृशं फलमा(व)प्नोति नात्र कार्यविचारणात्
original.edition: Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: As all rivers go to the ocean, so all dharmas dissolve in the Akulavīra, the support of all; those who take refuge in all dharmas do not find innate bliss (sahajānanda); seized by impurities and covered by the blindness of great Māyā, content with nets of scripture, they do not find the peaceful state, the partless guru of the Kaulas.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: When one sees the great Akulavīra everywhere, inside and outside, of one form in all that moves and stands — waveless, free of appearance and of distinctions of state, beyond the principles, spotless, all-knowing, full, imperishable, free of cause and effect, beyond Māyā, supportless, beyond 'is' and 'is not', where there is no mind, intellect, time, power, Śiva or senses — then all is samarasa and full, the Akulavīra alone.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: One in whom this liberation abides is freed from worldly bonds: for him there is no mother, father, kin or deity, no sacrifice, fasting, rite or distinction of caste; no recitation, worship, bathing, oblation or practice, no rule, ancestor-rite, pilgrimage or vow, no fruit of dharma or adharma. Abandoning worldly conduct and the made bonds of the pledges, the yogī is without conduct (nirācāra), free of the conduct of 'animals'.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: Those who argue — Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika, Buddhist arhats, the Somasiddhānta, Mīmāṃsā, the five streams, the Left, the Siddhānta and the Right, the Itihāsa and Purāṇa, the Bhūta and Gāruḍa tantras, all the Śaiva Āgamas with their rituals — all are full of conceptual constructs (vikalpa), false and meaningless; lacking the Akulavīra they do not free from saṃsāra.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: In the Kaula path there are two, the made (kṛtakā) and the innate (sahajā): the kuṇḍalī is to be known as the made, the innate abides in samarasa; the made consists in the relation of impelled and impeller and is brought down by seals and mantras, by oblation, ear-whispered mantra and incense.

original.text: कौलमार्गे द्वयो सन्ति कृतका सहजा तथा । कुण्डली कृतका ज्ञेया सहजा समरसे स्थिता प्रेर्यप्रेरकभावस्था कृतका साऽभिधीयते । ततः स पातयेद् भूमौ मुद्रामन्त्रैर्नियोजितैः आहुते पतने चान्ये कर्णजापेन धूपकैः । एतत् साध्यमिदं तत्त्वं (एतद्) ध्यानञ्च धारणा

paraphrase: As ghee is in curd, fire in wood, fragrance in a flower, oil in sesame, shade under a tree, joy in wine and light in a lamp, so the Akulavīra is present — in the lotus of kuṇḍalī and in every limb.

original.text: अकुले वीरे च सम्प्राप्ते सर्वमेतद्विनश्यति । दधिमध्ये यथा सर्पिः काष्ठे चाग्निः स्थितो यथा पुष्पे गन्धस्तिले तैलं वृक्षे छाया समाश्रिता । मद्यमध्ये यथानन्दं दीपे प्रभा समाश्रिता पद्ममध्ये च कुण्डल्या अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गमेव च । रक्तार्थाकुलवीरे (?) च तत्सर्वं विनियोजितम्

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: Going, standing, sleeping, waking, eating or in union, in fear, poverty or grief, the knower does not treat himself with remedies through sense-objects; he may act with all castes and does not discriminate food — so the yogī moves like fire in a forest.

original.text: न मुक्तो वै न च न मुक्तमे (?) मोक्षस्य च स्पृहा । गच्छंस्तिष्ठन् स्वपन् जाग्रद्भूञ्जानो मैथुनेऽपि वा भयदारिद्रशोकैश्च विविधैर्भक्षणैस्तथा । चिकित्सा नैव कुर्वीत इन्द्रियार्थैः कदाचन आचरेत् सर्ववर्णैस्तु न तु भक्ष्यं विचारयेत् । एवं स चरते योगी यथारण्ये हुताशनः

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: Those who have worshipped the guru with devotion for thousands of births, whose devotion to the circle of yoginīs is unshaken, obtain this great knowledge, the Akulavīra that gives liberation.

original.text: अप्रमेयनिराभासं धारणाध्यानवर्जितम् । येन जन्मसहस्राणि भक्त्या सम्पूजितो गुरुः ते लभन्ति महाज्ञानम् अकुलवीरन्तु मोक्षदम् । योगिनीराकिणीचक्रे यस्य भक्तिः सुनिश्चला

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: The Vedas, Siddhāntas and many kinds of śāstras are all delusion and bodily toil without purpose; the proud, seized by the conceit of learning and pondering many books, go to a bad end; how can the proud have knowledge even with hundreds of millions of books?

original.text: वेदसिद्धान्तशास्त्राणि नानाविधानि शिखानि च । तानि सर्वाणि मोहानि कायक्लेशैर्निरर्थकम् विद्याहङ्कारग्रस्तास्तु गर्विताः कुगतिं गताः । अनर्थेन च सन्तुष्टा बहुग्रन्थार्थचिन्तकाः गर्वितानां कुतो ज्ञानं ग्रन्थकोटिशतैरपि

paraphrase: Intentions and conceptions, the arts and works, the many powers in the world, the nether regions and alchemy (rasāyana) — even when directly obtained, one should never grasp them: all these are nets of bondage that lead down the lower path.

original.text: सङ्कल्पविकल्पञ्च कलाकर्माणि यानि च । सिद्धयो विविधा लोके पातालं च रसायनम् प्रत्यक्षञ्च यदा लब्धं न विगृह्णीयात् कदाचन । सर्वे ते पाशबद्धश्च अधोमार्गप्रदायकाः
original.edition: Akulavīratantra, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934), two recensions; Muktabodha e-text M00003

speaker: the Siddhanātha (Matsyendra)

paraphrase: The one who knows the Akulavīra as abiding in the body is freed from all bonds: for him there is no bondage of ritual, no caste or distinction of caste, no recitation, fire-worship, oblation, sacred seats or vows.
